where: Section 1, step list (first and second bullets)
problem: The steps say to store h₁ … hₙ and then to set the decoder's first state to 'the context vector', but the paragraph just above says plain seq2seq keeps only hₙ. A student following the steps will not know which of the stored states becomes c.
fix: Say explicitly: run the encoder and keep the last state hₙ as the context vector c = hₙ (the earlier states h₁ … h_{n−1} are produced but discarded in plain seq2seq).

problem: Section 2 scores the current decoder state s_t against the encoder states (eᵢ = score(s_t, hᵢ)), while Section 3 gives the Bahdanau score with s_{t−1}. Both are standard, but the chapter never says why the index differs, so a student may use s_t inside the Bahdanau formula and lose marks.
fix: Add one sentence: in Luong attention the score uses the state s_t already computed at this step; in Bahdanau attention the score uses the previous state s_{t−1}, because the context is needed to compute s_t itself. Use s_{t−1} in the Bahdanau formula, as given, and s_t for the generic/Luong recipe.

problem: The arithmetic is slightly off: 2.718 + 7.389 = 10.107, not 10.108. Small, but the numbers in a worked example must add up exactly as printed.

where: Section 3 (cost of Bahdanau) and Quiz Q6 answer
problem: Two cost statements are loose. (a) 'costs one matrix multiply per source position per step' — the projection U_a hᵢ does not depend on the decoder step and can be computed once for all source positions before decoding starts. (b) The claim that additive attention 'earns its keep when the decoder and encoder state sizes differ' is only true against plain dot attention; Luong's general form sᵗWh handles different sizes too, so the stated reason is incomplete.
fix: Say: Bahdanau needs a tanh over a projected sum at every step (the U_a hᵢ part can be precomputed, the W_a s_{t−1} and tanh parts cannot), which is more work per position per step than a dot product. For Q6, say additive attention helps when you want a learned nonlinear similarity, or when plain dot attention is used and the two state sizes differ (the general/bilinear form also handles that case).
